evals.prompt: Look up CVE-2021-44228 and tell me whether this repo is actually exposed.
evals.expected_output: Full enrichment profile for CVE-2021-44228 (aliases, CVSS v3.1/v4, EPSS, KEV status, affected ranges) plus a repository-impact table showing installed log4j-core version, source, and whether the version falls inside the vulnerable range.
expectations: Detects vuln-lookup mode from the CVE-* pattern and reads .vulnetix/memory.yaml at start to surface any prior state
Runs `vulnetix vdb vuln CVE-2021-44228 -o json | jq -f ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_lib/jq/vuln.jq` (never raw, to aggregate the 20 container views)
Runs `vulnetix vdb metrics CVE-2021-44228 -o json` in parallel and merges CVSS/EPSS/KEV data
Performs repo-impact analysis: globs manifest/lockfiles (pom.xml/gradle.lockfile for maven), greps for log4j-core, and reports installed version with source (lockfile vs manifest)
Prefers `vulnetix vdb vuln ... --reachability both` AST output when .reachability.queries_run > 0, otherwise falls back to grepping .affectedRoutines function names
Updates .vulnetix/memory.yaml with status: under_investigation, decision.choice: investigating, discovery.source: user and appends history event: lookup

evals.prompt: List every known vulnerability for express and tell me which ones affect the version we have installed — give me the first 20.
evals.expected_output: A filtered, paginated table of vulnerabilities for express showing ID, severity, Affects You?, Fixed In, prior memory status, and EPSS, with a summary of how many of N affect the installed version.
expectations: Detects package-vulns mode because 'express' does not match any vuln-id pattern
Resolves installed version via lockfile-priority chain (package-lock.json/yarn.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml) and labels the version source transparently
Runs `vulnetix vdb vulns express -o json --limit 20 | jq -f ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/_lib/jq/vulns.jq` honoring the 'first 20' pagination modifier
Filters returned vulns to the npm ecosystem detected in the repo and computes Affects You? Yes/No/Unknown against installed version range
Renders the table with columns ID/Severity/Affects You?/Fixed In/Status/EPSS and a summary `M of N affect your version`
Creates stub entries in .vulnetix/memory.yaml only for vulns that affect the installed version (status: under_investigation, discovery.source: scan, history event: discovered)

evals.prompt: GHSA-jfh8-3a1q-hjz9 just landed in a vendor advisory — is package-lock.json in the affected range, and is there a Dependabot alert open for it?
evals.expected_output: Vulnerability profile for GHSA-jfh8-3a1q-hjz9 with affected-package table, repo-impact assessment against package-lock.json, and the matching Dependabot alert state if gh is authenticated.
expectations: Identifies vuln-lookup mode from the GHSA-* pattern and loads .vulnetix/memory.yaml plus globs .vulnetix/scans/*.cdx.json for SBOM cross-reference
Calls `vulnetix vdb vuln GHSA-jfh8-3a1q-hjz9 -o json` piped through _lib/jq/vuln.jq, plus `vulnetix vdb metrics` in parallel
Checks `gh auth status 2>/dev/null` and queries `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependabot/alerts --jq` matching either security_advisory.cve_id or security_advisory.ghsa_id
Greps package-lock.json for affected packages and reports Direct vs Transitive relationship with installed version inside/outside the vulnerable range
Surfaces severity table (CVSS v3.1, v4.0, EPSS percentage, CISA KEV status/deadline) and Next Steps pointing to /vulnetix:exploits, /vulnetix:fix, /vulnetix:remediation
Updates .vulnetix/memory.yaml — merging aliases, refreshing severity/safe_harbour, appending history event: lookup, without overwriting existing status or decision
